title: Flash model quota exhaustion prevents fallback to available Pro model quota

linked_prs.title: fix: handle request retries and model fallback correctly
linked_prs.body:
## TLDR This pull request refactors the handling of API quota errors to be more robust and reliable. Previously, we relied on string matching to detect specific quota error messages. This change introduces a structured error parsing system that can correctly classify quota errors as either retryable (e.g., per-minute limits, small retry delays) or terminal (e.g., daily limits). The retry logic has been updated to use this new classification, ensuring that we only trigger model fallbacks for terminal quota errors and use the server-suggested delay for retryable errors when available. Also increased the max number of retries from 5 to 10 (found a lot more 503 errors from Gemini API succeeding within that). > [!NOTE] > Does not fix #9039. But with fewer incorrect model fallback attempts (which for auto model routing was previously terminating requests started with `flash`) it should help reduce the occurrence. ## Dive Deeper The core of this change is a new error classification system: 1. `parseGoogleApiError`: A new function in packages/core/src/errors.ts that can parse deeply nested and stringified Google API error responses, extracting the structured error details. 2. `TerminalQuotaError` and `RetryableQuotaError`: New custom error classes to represent different types of quota issues. 3. `classifyGoogleError`: A function that uses parseGoogleApiError to analyze 429 errors and wrap them in the appropriate custom error class. The retryWithBackoff function has been refactored to: - Catch `TerminalQuotaError` to trigger the `onPersistent429` fallback mechanism. - Catch `RetryableQuotaError` and use the `retryDelayMs` from the error for a more accurate backoff period. The UI hook `useQuotaAndFallback` has also been updated to use `instanceof TerminalQuotaError` for its logic, simplifying the code and removing the need for the old isProQuotaExceededError and isGenericQuotaExceededError functions, which have been deleted. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### Using GCA auth - Set `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=aipp-internal-testing (or whatever)` and run `gemini-cli` from this branch, login with oauth. You should be able to make a lot of queries before seeing automatic fallback error. -
Run this script for a while to exhaust the pro model quota. ``` #!/bin/bash for i in {1..2000} do echo "Request #$i" curl -i -sN -X POST \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \ -H 'x-goog-user-project: aipp-internal-testing' \ --json '{ "project":"aipp-internal-testing", "model":"gemini-2.5-pro", "request":{ "contents": { "role": "user", "parts": [ { "text": "Hi" }, ] } } }' \ https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:streamGenerateContent done echo "Done." ```
- Issue a request on gemini-cli, you should see the model fallback error. ### Using Gemini API key - Restrict quota manually to force 429 errors. Go to [this](https://pantheon.corp.google.com/apis/api/generativelanguage.googleapis.com/quotas?pageState=(%22allQuotasTable%22:(%22p%22:0,%22f%22:%22%255B%257B_22k_22_3A_22Has%2520override_22_2C_22t_22_3A11_2C_22v_22_3A_22_5C_22True_5C_22_22_2C_22s_22_3Atrue_2C_22i_22_3A_22hasConsumerOverride_22%257D_2C%257B_22k_22_3A_22Name_22_2C_22t_22_3A10_2C_22v_22_3A_22_5C_22GenerateContent%2520input%2520token%2520count%2520limit%2520per%2520model_5C_22_22_2C_22i_22_3A_22displayName_22%257D_2C%257B_22k_22_3A_22Dimensions%2520%2528e.g.%2520location%2529_22_2C_22t_22_3A10_2C_22v_22_3A_22_5C_22model_3Agemini-2.5-pro_5C_22_22_2C_22s_22_3Atrue_2C_22i_22_3A_22displayDimensions_22%257D%255D%22,%22c%22:%5B%22metricName%22,%22limitName%22,%22monitoredResource%22%5D))) link and select the project for which you've created the Gemini API key. - Override the value to be something low like 50,000. - Run `gemini-cli` from this branch, use this Gemini API key for auth, and start making requests. - Requests should appear to be taking a lot longer (due to retries from the 429 error code `retryInfo` objects) instead of failing. > [!NOTE] > Right now even retryable errors are run for a max of 10 attempts (same as other error codes). We can consider retrying these errors for a longer number than other error codes. ## Testing Matrix | | 🍏 | 🪟 | 🐧 | |----------|-----|-----|-----| | npm run | ❓ | ❓ | ✅ | | npx | ❓ | ❓ | ❓ | | Docker | ❓ | ❓ | ❓ | | Podman | ❓ | - | - | | Seatbelt | ❓ | - | - | Fixes: - #9248 - #5119 - #3510 - #1088 - #4186
